text:
tyler: seeing a spike in gRPC streaming stalls out of eu-west1 — ~5% of streaming embed sessions hang and then get a RESET after ~110-130s. client -> alb -> edge-proxy -> inference-pool. anyone seen this?

maria: saw a matching blip in dashboards, higher tail latency + some 502/GRPC_CANCEL. span traces show no application errors, bytes_sent flatlines during the hang.

ashok: poked edge-proxy logs, there are repeated h2 window warnings and window_update frames not being propagated downstream. proxy has a per-stream window clamp we added last year for fairness.

kevin: interesting — ALB idle timeout is 60s in that region, LB healthchecks normal. resets are ~2min so maybe something retransmits? also NAT ephemeral ports for that AZ were close to limit earlier.

maria: attached a short trace snippet (repro) — client kept sending small chunks, server stalled waiting on WINDOW_UPDATE. then ALB emits FIN.

ashok: reproduced locally: when we clamp the stream window to 64KB and the client keeps a long-running request with low throughput, the server-side runtime stalls waiting for more window. If ALB buffers and doesn't forward mid-stream window_update, the net effect is deadlock.

kevin: do we have code showing ALB behavior w.r.t WINDOW_UPDATE? I thought ALB proxies h2 correctly.

ashok: ALB forwards frames but we observed a codepath where it aggregates frames and passes through only when a data chunk crosses its internal buffer threshold — that delays window_update visibility. Putting that together with our clamp yields a stall until ALB triggers connection-level keepalive/close.

tyler: this is bad for GPU batching — streams stuck in limbo hold KV caches and prevent other requests from using that slot, causing batch size drop and autoscaler reactions. noticed a drop in throughput on the affected pool.

ops-lead: can we mitigate quickly? options: relax clamp on edge-proxy for streaming endpoints, ensure ALB has smaller buffering thresholds, enable per-stream keepalive pings so ALB doesn't aggregate, or route streaming traffic through a different ALB config.

maria: quick test suggestion: flip edge-proxy clamp to 256KB for a single canary node and watch eu-west1 tail. also toggle socket keepalive to 30s for that service.

ashok: agreed. I'll spin a canary tomorrow morning and add extra logging of WINDOW_UPDATE frames. command I ran locally:

```
# tail logs and filter for window events
kubectl logs -f pod/edge-proxy-0 -c proxy | grep -i WINDOW_UPDATE
```

kevin: I'll open a ticket with ALB support to confirm buffering semantics and ask about any recent changes in that region.

sre-bot: incident created: I-2026-2093 — "h2 window-clamp stalls in eu-west1". paging list: @ops-lead @ashok.

ops-lead: immediate plan: 1) canary relax clamp (ashok) 2) enable aggressive keepalive for streaming service (maria) 3) ALB ticket (kevin). follow-ups: metrics to monitor: stalled_streams, avg_window_size, gpu_batch_fill.

tyler: thanks — please post results in this thread and tag infra-oncall if the canary impacts latency.

maria: canary flipped at 1772003600, early signs: stalled_streams down from 5% -> 1.2% on canary nodes. will let it run 30m then consider rollout.

ashok: added debug that logs WINDOW_UPDATE delta per stream, pushing to temporary metric stream. will dump samples in 30m.

kevin: ALB support replied — they acknowledged a progressive buffering optimization rolled last week in eu-west1. they recommend enabling HTTP/2 stream-level window forwarding via config flag (internal). I've asked for timeline on region-wide rollout.

ops-lead: great. set follow-up for postmortem if this recurs. thanks team. :thumbsup:
